name: Bab-el-Mandeb
note: Arabic for 'Gate of Grief,' named for its dangerous currents.
description: The Bab-el-Mandeb — the 'Gate of Grief,' named for its dangerous currents and reefs — is the southern door of the Red Sea, and with it the southern door of the Suez route between Europe and Asia. Between Yemen on the Arabian shore and Djibouti and Eritrea on the African one, the strait links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. Nearly everything that transits the Suez Canal passes here too, which gives a passage barely thirty kilometres wide an outsized grip on world trade, felt keenly whenever the region's conflicts reach the water.
